title: Banner Band's reputation and Bunk Johnson's later years
summary: Duhé says the band was unbeatable in New Iberia and talks about Bunk's last years and the hardships of the road.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: New Orleans couldn't come in in New Iberia then. You really like that band? Oh yeah, we killed New Orleans. I mean, we killed till it's there. Don't come in New Iberia, not there when we was there. Now, don't Bunk always want to play with you again? The last few years. Bill Bucking, that last album, he came right here. Two or three times. Flood Rain. You know, you know, the old one can play those numbers on the one. He named him. All the more, the only one. The old Redback Bucking. Oh, he had one. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. You see, everything happens for the best.
Yes, sir. Sometimes, well, either way, you've been here and been happy.
Yeah, I've had mine, so I'll let the other fellas have a chance.
George has been traveling around lately, but he's not so well. I guess the road hasn't agreed very well with him either. So it's tough to be on the road. On the road, yeah.
Unless you know how to take care of yourself. You've got to be like this guy and I, see if we know the road question. It requires a meal to rest. I'm telling you. Meals and rest. I don't get it.
